newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Southcorp confirms on track for forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Southcorp confirms on track for forecasts.

text.p: Packaging, appliance and wine group Southcorp Holdings Ltd chief executive officer Graham Kraehe said on Thursday he still expected the company to achieve profits in line with market expectations for the year just ended on June 30.
"I can confirm that we expect to be in line with market expectations for the past year," Kraehe told an Australian Institute of Comany Directors' luncheon.
Kraehe said market expectations were for earnings growth of between 10 percent and 15 percent in the 1996/97 year and again in 1997/98.
Kraehe had said previously that analysts were expecting a net profit before abnormals for the 1996/97 year of about A$130 million.
He said on Thursday that some of the group's growth in its core packaging business would be funded by planned divestments as the focus continued to be on core businesses.
The outlook for the group's wine business was "exceptional", Kraehe said.
"The strong international (wine) demand growth, particularly in the United States offers great prospects for us," he said.
"We will continue to invest in the wine business to extend the potential for double digit earnings growth well into the next century," Kraehe said.
"We are close to finalising the next step in the international expansion of Southcorp Wine," he said.

Kraehe said he was confident the appliance division's performance had bottomed out "but in the medium term our focus will remain on improving Appliance profit levels off the existing Australian investment base."
